question: With which of the following does Article 72 of the Constitution of India deal? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (21/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: Composition and jurisdiction of Supreme Court of India
Right to freedom of speech
Pardoning power of the President
Appointment of Prime Minister
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Pardoning power of the President

Explanation:
Article 72 of the Indian Constitution grants the President the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment, and to suspend, remit, or commute sentences. This power applies to offenses against Union laws, sentences by court-martial, and death sentences. The President's pardoning power is subject to judicial review, as established in the case of Kehar Singh vs Union of India. It differs from the Governor's pardoning power under Article 161, as the President can pardon death sentences while the Governor cannot. Article 72(1) details this power, which is a key feature of the executive authority of the President.

☛ Which article deals with the President's pardoning power? → Article 72
☛ Which landmark case is related to the President's pardoning power? → Kehar Singh vs Union of India
☛ Which article deals with the Governor's pardoning power? → Article 161
☛ Is the President's pardoning power subject to judicial review? → Yes
☛ Which sentences can the President pardon? → Union offenses, court-martial, death sentences

solution_hi:

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 72 राष्ट्रपति को क्षमादान, दण्डादेश को स्थगित, विराम या परिहार करने और सजा को कम या बदलने की शक्ति प्रदान करता है। यह शक्ति संघीय कानूनों के विरुद्ध अपराधों, सैन्य न्यायालयों द्वारा दी गई सजाओं और मृत्युदंड के मामलों पर लागू होती है। राष्ट्रपति की यह शक्ति न्यायिक समीक्षा के अधीन है, जैसा कि केहर सिंह बनाम भारत संघ मामले में स्पष्ट हुआ। अनुच्छेद 72 राज्यपाल की क्षमादान शक्ति (अनुच्छेद 161) से भिन्न है, क्योंकि राष्ट्रपति मृत्युदंड के मामलों में भी क्षमा कर सकता है, जबकि राज्यपाल नहीं कर सकता। यह शक्ति अनुच्छेद 72(1) में वर्णित है।

question: What is the motto of the Supreme Court of India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (21/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: Equal Justice for All
Yato Dharmastato Jayah
Satyamev Jayate
Yogakshemam Vahamyaham
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Yato Dharmastato Jayah

Explanation:
The motto of the Supreme Court of India is 'Yato Dharmastato Jayah', a Sanskrit phrase meaning 'Where there is dharma (righteousness), there is victory'. It is derived from the epic Mahabharata and is inscribed below the Ashoka Chakra on the emblem of the Supreme Court. The motto reflects the role of the judiciary in upholding justice and righteousness, leading to truth and victory. Among the other options, 'Satyamev Jayate' is the national motto of India, 'Equal Justice for All' represents a principle of the court, and 'Yogakshemam Vahamyaham' is a verse from the Bhagavad Gita indicating the welfare role of the state.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ From which epic is Yato Dharmastato Jayah taken? → Mahabharata
☛ What is the national motto of India? → Satyamev Jayate
☛ What is inscribed on the Supreme Court emblem? → Ashoka Chakra and the motto
☛ What does Yato Dharmastato Jayah mean? → Where there is righteousness, there is victory

question: The President of India is elected by: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (27/03/2021) Shift 1)
options: Electoral College
Direct election
System of Universal adult Franchise
Members of the Parliament
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Electoral College

Explanation:
The President of India is elected by an Electoral College consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) and elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of states. The election follows the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote. Voting is conducted by secret ballot. The value of votes of MPs and MLAs is not equal; it is determined based on the population of states. The Supreme Court is the final authority to decide disputes related to the Presidential election. This indirect election method ensures fair representation of both the states and the Union.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What is the voting system in Presidential election? → Single transferable vote
☛ How many types of voters are in Presidential election? → Two: MPs and MLAs
☛ How is vote value determined in Presidential election? → Based on population
☛ Who is the final authority for Presidential election disputes? → Supreme Court
☛ What type of voting is used in Presidential election? → Secret ballot

question: In the late 18th century, which Indian cities rose in importance as the Presidency cities? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (27/03/2021) Shift 1)
options: Calcutta (kolkata), Bombay (Mumbai) and Delhi
Calcutta (Kolkata), Bombay (Mumbai) and Madras (Chennai)
Delhi, Bombay (Mumbai) and Madras(Chennai)
Calcutta (Kolkata), Delhi and Madras (Chennai)
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Calcutta (Kolkata), Bombay (Mumbai) and Madras (Chennai)

Explanation:
In the late 18th century, the British East India Company established three major presidencies in India. These presidency cities were Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras. Calcutta served as the capital of the Bengal Presidency, Bombay of the Bombay Presidency, and Madras of the Madras Presidency. These cities developed as administrative, commercial, and military centers. Delhi was not a presidency city at that time; it later became the capital under British rule in 1911. These three cities played a crucial role in the modern development of India.

☛ When did Delhi become the capital? → 1911

question: When the Right to Property was removed from our 'fundamental rights' and was made a 'legal right'? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (27/03/2021) Shift 1)
options: 1978
1968
1976
1979
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1978

Explanation:
The Right to Property was originally a fundamental right under Article 31 in Part-III of the Indian Constitution. It was removed from fundamental rights and made a legal right under Article 300A by the 44th Constitutional Amendment in 1978. This amendment was passed during the tenure of Prime Minister Morarji Desai and came into effect in 1979. Now, no person can be deprived of their property except by authority of law, but it is no longer a fundamental right.

☛ Which Amendment made Right to Property a legal right? → 44th Amendment (1978)
☛ Under which Article is the legal Right to Property now? → Article 300A
☛ Who was the Prime Minister during the 44th Amendment? → Morarji Desai
☛ Which Amendment restricted judicial review? → 42nd Amendment

question: The quorum required in the Rajya Sabha is: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (27/03/2021) Shift 2)

50

solution:

question: Which article of the Constitution of India covers 'Right to Life'? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (27/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: Article 20
Article 34
Article 21
Article 32
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 21

Explanation:
Article 21 of the Indian Constitution is part of Part III (Fundamental Rights). It states that no person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to the procedure established by law. The Supreme Court has expansively interpreted 'Right to Life' to include the right to live with dignity, health, education, clean environment, and livelihood. Article 20 deals with protection against conviction for offences, Article 34 restricts rights during martial law, and Article 32 provides the right to constitutional remedies. Therefore, the Right to Life is enshrined in Article 21.

question: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution deals with the protection of the interests of minorities? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (01/04/2021) Shift 2)
options: Article 29
​Article 20
​Article 21A
​Article 24
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 29

Explanation:
Article 29 of the Indian Constitution deals with the protection of the interests of minorities. It is part of Part 3 (Fundamental Rights) under the heading 'Cultural and Educational Rights'. Article 29(1) states that any section of citizens residing in any part of India having a distinct language, script, or culture has the right to conserve the same. Article 29(2) provides that no citizen shall be denied admission into any educational institution maintained by the State or receiving aid out of State funds on grounds only of religion, race, caste, or language. This provision safeguards the cultural identity and educational opportunities of minority communities.

Explanation:
The soul of the Indian Constitution is the 'Fundamental Rights'. They are enshrined in Part III (Articles 12–35) of the Constitution. Fundamental Rights protect citizens from arbitrary state action and form the bedrock of democracy. Dr. B. R. Ambedkar called them the soul of the Constitution because they ensure individual liberty and equality. These rights are justiciable, meaning citizens can approach the Supreme Court if they are violated. Fundamental Rights include Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies. Article 32, which grants the right to move the Supreme Court, is itself a fundamental right and is described as the heart of the Constitution.

question: Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (01/04/2021) Shift 2)
options: President
Prime Ministe
Lok Sabha
Rajya Sabha
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lok Sabha

Explanation:
According to Article 75(3) of the Indian Constitution, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. This is a fundamental principle of the parliamentary system of government, where the executive (Council of Ministers) is accountable to the legislature (Lok Sabha). If the Lok Sabha passes a vote of no-confidence against the Council of Ministers, the entire council must resign. The President is the constitutional head but acts on the advice of the Prime Minister. The Rajya Sabha cannot bring a no-confidence motion. The Prime Minister is the head of the council, but collective responsibility is towards the Lok Sabha.

question: Sarkaria Commission was set up in 1983 to: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (03/04/2021) Shift 1)
options: examine the feasibility of replacing the existing multiple taxes by an integrated Goods and Services Tax
examine the relationship and balance of power between state and central governments and suggest changes
recommend measures to clear backlog of cases in courts
make recommendations regarding reservations in civil services and posts
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is examine the relationship and balance of power between state and central governments and suggest changes

Explanation:
The Sarkaria Commission was set up in 1983 to review the center-state relations in India. It was chaired by Justice Ranjit Singh Sarkaria. The commission examined issues like Article 356, the role of governors, and financial relations. It recommended preserving the central government's strength while granting more autonomy to states. It also proposed the formation of the Inter-State Council, which was established in 1990. The commission aimed to maintain a balance of power between the center and states, and its recommendations remain a key reference for federal relations in India.

question: The commonwealth of nations, normally known as ‘The Commonwealth’ is a: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (03/04/2021) Shift 1)
options: political association
human rights association
social organisation
economic association
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is political association

Explanation:
The Commonwealth of Nations is an intergovernmental political association of mostly former British Empire territories. It was established through the Statute of Westminster in 1931 and formalized with the London Declaration in 1949. Currently, it has 56 member states, with King Charles III as the head of 15 realms. Its main purposes include promoting democracy, peace, and development. It is a voluntary association with no constitution, operating based on shared values and goals. Commonwealth members cooperate in areas like trade, education, and human rights, but it is primarily a political forum for dialogue.

question: Which of the following states is NOT governed by 6th schedule of Indian Constitution?  (RRB NTPC CBT-I (03/04/2021) Shift 1)
options: Arunachal Pradesh
Mizoram
Tripura
Assam
solution:

Explanation:
The Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution provides for the administration of tribal areas in four states: Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram, and Tripura. It allows the formation of Autonomous District Councils with legislative powers over land, forests, water, and social customs. Arunachal Pradesh is not covered under the Sixth Schedule; its tribal areas are designated as Scheduled Tribal Areas with a different administrative framework. The Sixth Schedule ensures tribal autonomy in hilly and remote regions of the Northeast, distinct from the Fifth Schedule applicable in other states. Understanding this distinction is crucial for governance and constitutional provisions.

question: Who presides over the first meeting of a newly constituted Lok Sabha? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (05/04/2021) Shift 1)
options: Prime Minister
Speaker
Protem Speaker
President
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Protem Speaker

Explanation:
The first meeting of a newly constituted Lok Sabha is presided over by the Protem Speaker. According to Article 94 of the Constitution, when the Lok Sabha is dissolved or newly elected, the President appoints one of the senior-most members as the Protem Speaker. The Protem Speaker administers the oath of office to the newly elected members and conducts the election of the new Speaker. Until the permanent Speaker is elected, the Protem Speaker manages the proceedings of the House. This practice ensures a smooth transition and upholds democratic traditions in the functioning of the lower house of Parliament.

solution:

Explanation:
The Constituent Assembly of India was formed in 1946. Its permanent chairman was Dr. Rajendra Prasad, while the vice-chairman was H. C. Mookherjee. H. C. question_hi: भारतीय संविधान लिखने वाली संविधान सभा के उपाध्यक्ष कौन थे? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (05/04/2021) Shift 2)
options_hi: जी दुर्गाबाई देशमुख
राजेंद्र प्रसाद
एच सी मुखर्जी
जैपाल सिंह
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है एच सी मुखर्जी

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान सभा का गठन 1946 में हुआ था। इसके स्थायी अध्यक्ष डॉ. राजेन्द्र प्रसाद थे, जबकि उपाध्यक्ष एच. सी. मुखर्जी थे। एच. सी. मुखर्जी एक प्रमुख शिक्षाविद् और राजनीतिज्ञ थे, जिन्होंने संविधान निर्माण में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई। संविधान सभा में कुल 389 सदस्य थे, जिनमें से 292 प्रांतों से, 93 रियासतों से और 4 विशेष वर्गों से चुने गए थे। संविधान सभा ने 26 नवंबर 1949 को संविधान को अपनाया और 26 जनवरी 1950 को इसे लागू किया गया।
